title: Grateful Dead Live at Reed's Ranch on 1969-07-03
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Tascam SS-R05 -> Samplitude Pro X Suite -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of the rare July‑3‑1969 Colorado Springs show with solid pedal‑steel moments and strong early country‑rock performances; recording is clear but has a few early glitches.
ai_review.review: The set showcases Jerry’s experimental pedal‑steel work on songs like “Slewfoot,” “Green Grass of Home,” and the extended “He Was a Friend of Mine,” while the band delivers an earnest early‑Dead country‑rock vibe. The soundboard source is generally clean and well‑pitched, though listeners note brief equipment hiccups in the opening minutes of “Lovelight.” Overall the show is praised for its unique repertoire despite some rough edges.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give five‑star praise for performance and sound quality; one moderate review notes minor flaws, yielding a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and well‑pitched after patching; a slight waver and brief equipment issues in the first ~5 min of “Lovelight,” but overall crisp with minimal audience bleed.

standout_songs: He Was a Friend of Mine (Just a Hand to Hold)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑summer ‘69 country‑rock set played at dawn; the band experiments with pedal steel and leans into traditional tunes, delivering a relaxed yet energetic flow despite some sloppy moments.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Experimenting on pedal steel; his playing adds interesting texture (not virtuoso but effective) and he returns to vocals later in the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Provides sweet vocal harmonies, especially on “Green Green Grass of Home.”
band_member_comments.Drums: Frantic drumming noted during “Sitting on Top of the World” and other high‑energy moments.
